_doc: Unique-index exemptions for the keys instruments (multi-space plan V204 §2.4 'Unique keys and upserts', step 2.0e, V5-SPACETENANCYKEY-001).

A unique index on an S, D or base-capable C table (class from lambda/tenancy-classes.json) must carry the tenancy key, or be listed here with its class and a one-line reason. The rule, per arm: S: a key column is workspace_id or the table's tenancy column. D: a key column is workspace_id or the tenancy column; on 'D via plot' tables space_id or plot_id (§2.2); or the leading key column alone carries a single-column FK into an S or D table. C base + private: a key column is workspace_id, or the predicate holds a bare top-level is_base conjunct (no OR). An index with NULLS NOT DISTINCT never passes by rule.

Read by the gate post_s_unique_indexes_carry_workspace (migrations/v5-tenancykeys-001: gates.yml and 0a-stamp.sql carry these rows as a VALUES list, kept equal by lambda/tenancy-keys.static.test.js) and by that test (the closed world against tests/tenancy-unique-indexes.prod.json, and every ON CONFLICT arbiter the SQL census finds).

Entry keys: table, index, class (2-6), reason; route (class 5: the writer files whose conflict path 5.3 reads); row (the plan step that re-keys, decides or removes it; class 6: a 5.3 row); pending (a schema_version stamp: the index is not yet applied, so its absence from the snapshot is tolerated). Sorted by table, then index. An entry for an index that passes by rule, or that is absent and not pending, fails the test.

Day one (2.0e): recon B §4's list (the 24 keys on S candidates that do not carry workspace_id, re-read live 2026-10-19, unchanged) plus the D and base-capable C tables' keys, read live the same day (recon B §4 did not cover them).

classes.1: single-column primary key on id. By rule in the gate and the test, never an entry (N14: no other single-column widening).
classes.2: PK-leading composite: unique by its primary-key column already.
classes.3: leading column is an FK to the row's Space-owned parent, or a scope id bound to one; named one by one.
classes.4: C rows on a mixed table (catalog identity: the system singleton, one catalog entity per catalog row).
classes.5: client idempotency key whose conflict path returns nothing; each is read at its route by the 5.3 lane and re-keyed (workspace_id, key) if the conflict path returns or reveals the existing row.
classes.6: temporary: a pending re-key naming its 5.3 row; or the dormant global key locations_qr_code_slug_key (SIA-51).
